summary: Kang-nam Oh works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yün-hua Jan (attested 1976), and held a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

Kang-yuan Sung specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary, where he studied under MA supervisor Anthony W. Barber (attested 1999) and teachers Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris, and later served as a non-regular staff member (嘱託) at Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies. He served at Rissho University as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

Kanoko Tanaka specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied under traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi and held a position as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).
Kanti Chandra Pandey (1903–1971) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He founded the University of Lucknow and held a post there (attested 1950).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) studied at the universities of Delhi (MA), Michigan (MA), and Banaras Hindu University (PhD). She taught at Delhi and BHU, founded IGNCA—serving as trustee, Academic Director, and chairperson—and chaired the India International Centre.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao (born 1955) studied at Panjab University, DAV College Chandigarh, Delhi University, and Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman. He taught at Kirori Mal College and became a professor at Delhi in 1995.

Karandagolle Sobhitha specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil from the University of Peradeniya by 2018, where he was a temporary lecturer (2011–2015), and served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2015–2021).

Karel Glaser (1845–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Vienna (PhD 1883), including under Georg Bühler (~1880–1883). He taught at Stadtgymnasium Trieste from 1880 to 1900.

Karel Oštir (1888–1973), an Indologist and linguist, studied under Paul Kretschmer at the University of Vienna and Rudolf Meringer at the University of Graz (PhD 1919). He served as a professor of Indo-European philology at the University of Ljubljana from 1922 to 1958.
Karel Přikryl (1718–1785) was an Indologist and linguist. He taught at Rachol Seminary (~1756–1761) and served as Rector of the Jesuit College in Hradec Králové in 1768.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) studied at Masaryk University and Palacký University Olomouc. He founded Masaryk University, held posts at Palacký, Cambridge, and Masaryk, and served as lecturer in Indian philosophy at Durham University (1969–1990).

Karen Christina Lang specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as professor at the University of Virginia.

Karen Katsumoto specializes in Buddhist studies. She held a position as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. A religious studies scholar, she served as professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976–2009) and held posts at Harvard, Berkeley, and other institutions.

Karen Nelson Villanueva completed her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies in religious studies and other fields. She studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago, where she taught Sally McAra.

Karen O'Brien-Kop, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, completed her PhD and served as a senior teaching fellow at SOAS. She held lectureships at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020) and King's College London (2022).
